text.p: Weak U.K. clothing demand and difficulties in the U.S. will hit half-year results from troubled clothing groups Courtaulds Textiles Plc and Coats Viyella Plc next week, analysts said on Friday.

Courtaulds Textiles Plc, which issued a profit warning at its annual general meeting in May, is expected to break even or show a small loss in the six months to June 30 compared with pretax profit of 6.4 million stg a year earlier, according to a consensus of analysts' forecasts.
The dividend is forecast to be maintained at 5.2 pence, analysts said.

Coats Viyella, which announced a shock 50 million stg restructuring plan in March, is forecast by analysts to post pretax profit of between 39 and 43.2 million stg, down sharply from 70.8 million a year before. The dividend is expected to be held at 3.7 pence.
One analyst, who asked not to be named, said forecasting for Coats is difficult because noone knows how much of the restructuring charge will fall in the first half of the year.
Courtaulds has been hit by destocking by U.S. retailers and lingerie manufacturers.

One analyst who asked not to be named said U.S. retailers last year "went overboard for Christmas, and the result was a lot of stock washing around in the last quarter of 1995," and hanging over into the first quarter of 1996.
The group said in May that U.S. sales in the first half of the year were down 30 percent from a year before.
Coats Viyella has also responded to its problems with a radical shake-up, replacing chief executive Noel Jervis and embarking on a string of non-core disposals.
Another analyst, who also asked not to be identified, said however that both companies should be able to reflect improved UK trading conditions in their interim statements.
"With consumer confidence improving and no repeat of last year's exceptional weather we should hear better news on current trading,"she said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
